headline: Levers are force multipliers—trading distance for power to move the immovable
universal_truth: Leverage exists everywhere; small inputs can create large outputs when positioned correctly
fun_facts: Archimedes said: 'Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I shall move the world'
Your arm is a lever—your elbow is the fulcrum, muscles apply force, and your hand moves objects
A crowbar can multiply your force by 10 times or more
discussion_questions: Where do you see levers in everyday life?
What's the trade-off when using a lever?
Where in life can you apply 'leverage' to multiply your efforts?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A boulder weighs a ton. You weigh much less. Yet with a long enough lever, you could lift that boulder with one hand. Levers are force multipliers—simple machines that let weak humans move heavy worlds.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If levers multiply force, do they create energy from nothing? That would violate physics. So what's the trade-off? Where does the extra force come from?

options.text: Levers trade distance for force—you push farther to lift something a shorter distance
options.response: Yes. No free lunch—you push through a longer arc to move the load a shorter distance. Same energy, different arrangement.

options.text: Levers store energy in the fulcrum and release it on the other side
options.response: The fulcrum enables the trade-off, but the real exchange is distance for force...

q1.title: The Trade-Off
q1.script: Levers don't create force—they redistribute it. Push down one meter to lift something 10 centimeters, and you've multiplied your force by 10. You do the same total work, just spread differently. Physics always balances.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Trade-Off"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Your Body's Levers
q2.script: Your skeleton is full of levers. Your forearm is a lever—elbow as fulcrum, bicep providing force, hand doing work. Your jaw is a lever. Even your skull pivots on your spine as a lever. You're a machine made of levers.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Three Classes
q3.script: Levers come in three classes based on where the fulcrum, effort, and load sit. Seesaws, wheelbarrows, and fishing rods are all levers—but each places these elements differently. Same principle, many configurations.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Leverage exists everywhere. In physics and in life, small inputs can create large outputs when positioned correctly. Find the fulcrum, apply force at the right point, and move the immovable.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 113. Tomorrow, we'll discover how to lift heavy things easily—pulleys. Until then, notice the levers around you, including the ones in your own body.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Life Leverage - Find Your Fulcrum
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply the concept of leverage to life situations
growTrack.activity: Where in your life could you apply leverage—small inputs creating large outputs? A skill that opens many doors? A relationship that multiplies opportunities? Identify one area where you could find better leverage.
